topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: It frames the lecture by introducing the learning outcomes and the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Proliferative signaling pathways and oncogenic mutations
topics.groupedBecause: They describe how mutations in signaling cascades, including Wnt/beta-catenin and receptor tyrosine kinase pathways, drive sustained cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation block in hematopoietic and epithelial cancers
topics.groupedBecause: They illustrate how an arrest in terminal cell differentiation contributes to tumor development in both leukemias and colorectal carcinomas.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis through p53 and Bcl-2 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: It examines how cancer cells avoid programmed cell death through alterations in p53 signaling and the balance of Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and stress responses
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how telomere shortening triggers senescence, how cancer cells bypass this barrier to achieve immortality, and how cellular stress pathways converge to protect genome integrity.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how cancer cells alter metabolic pathways, shifting toward aerobic glycolysis and generating oncometabolites that promote epigenetic dysregulation.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and vascular supply
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the mechanisms and timing of the angiogenic switch required to provide developing tumors with blood supply and oxygen.

topics.label: Mechanisms, detection, and genomics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the multi-step metastatic cascade, the clinical application of circulating tumor cells, seed-and-soil dynamics, and the genomic characteristics of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: It provides closing remarks summarizing the hallmarks of cancer and concludes the lecture.
